_why_two_claims: AGREEMENT asks whether the engines compute the same thing; RECOVERY asks whether they compute the right thing. Neither implies the other.

truth.source: the fixture's data-generating process: variance components 64 (subject), 9 (rater), 16 (error)

agreement.claim: both engines report the same ICC(A,1), ICC(C,1) and their intervals
agreement._note: Observed spread on the committed fixture: 0, irr against Python's written-out mean squares. harness/agreement_examples.test.py rebuilds the mean squares from explicit sums of squares and shows consistency exceeds absolute agreement by more than 0.03 on average.

recovery.claim: the estimates are close to the fixture's

calibration.rule: about 1.3 times the measured 99th percentile miss, rounded up
calibration.limits: With 4 raters ICC(A,1) is imprecise (miss 0.18); the tolerance separates it from zero, not from ICC(C,1). Measured by harness/agreement_examples.test.py over seeds 0 to 99 (MALLARD_SEEDS=100); CI reruns it on seeds 0 to 49 at the same order statistic (owner decisions E5, E6).
